mu-dc79ab25.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression?
mu-dc79ab25.explanation: All muscles of facial expression develop from the 2nd pharyngeal arch and are supplied by the facial nerve. The muscles of mastication come from the 1st arch and are supplied by the mandibular nerve (V3).

mu-bfc1e2e0.stem: Which nerve supplies the muscles of mastication?
mu-bfc1e2e0.explanation: Masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoid develop from the 1st pharyngeal arch and are supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve.

mu-5756c484.stem: Which muscle of mastication can be felt hardening in the cheek when the teeth are clenched?
mu-5756c484.explanation: Masseter runs from the zygomatic arch to the outer surface of the mandibular ramus; it is one of the strongest jaw-closing muscles and is easily felt in the cheek when the teeth are clenched.

mu-77190f39.stem: Which fan-shaped muscle of mastication lies in the temple region?
mu-77190f39.explanation: Temporalis is the fan-shaped muscle filling the temporal fossa; its fibres converge on the coronoid process; it closes the jaw and its posterior fibres retract it.

mu-9fd66965.stem: Which muscle purses the lips (whistling, kissing)?
mu-9fd66965.explanation: Orbicularis oris is the sphincter muscle encircling the mouth; it closes and purses the lips. Buccinator presses the cheek against the teeth.

mu-a136b758.stem: How many extraocular muscles move the eyeball?
mu-a136b758.explanation: The eyeball is moved by four recti (superior, inferior, medial, lateral) and two obliques (superior, inferior). Levator palpebrae superioris raises the eyelid and does not move the eyeball.

mu-93236a42.stem: Which prominent muscle on the side of the neck runs from behind the ear to the sternum and clavicle?
mu-93236a42.explanation: Sternocleidomastoid runs from the mastoid process to the manubrium and medial clavicle; it is an important surface landmark dividing the neck into anterior and posterior triangles.

mu-17cc2434.stem: Which thin, broad muscle of facial expression covers the front of the neck under the skin?
mu-17cc2434.explanation: Platysma is a superficial muscle of facial expression running from the upper chest to the mandible and corner of the mouth; it is supplied by the cervical branch of the facial nerve.

mu-2e1f0cc1.stem: Which superficial muscle of the upper back shrugs (elevates) the shoulders?
mu-2e1f0cc1.explanation: The upper fibres of trapezius elevate the scapula (shrugging); the middle fibres retract it and the lower fibres depress it. Levator scapulae also helps elevation.

mu-85f6c024.stem: Which is the broadest muscle of the back?
mu-85f6c024.explanation: Latissimus dorsi is a broad triangular muscle covering the lower back and loin; it extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm (the climbing and swimming muscle).

mu-c0a357d6.stem: Which muscle group runs along both sides of the spine and keeps the trunk upright?
mu-c0a357d6.explanation: From lateral to medial, erector spinae consists of the iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis columns; it extends the spine and maintains upright posture.

mu-e2ce0107.stem: Which is the most important (principal) muscle of respiration?
mu-e2ce0107.explanation: In quiet breathing the diaphragm does most of the work of inspiration; when it contracts its dome descends and the vertical diameter of the thoracic cavity increases.

mu-37ce2eca.stem: Which is the largest muscle on the front of the chest?
mu-37ce2eca.explanation: Pectoralis major is the fan-shaped muscle covering the front of the chest; it adducts, medially rotates and flexes the arm.

mu-9f5f0fd6.stem: Which muscle gives the 'six-pack' appearance of the anterior abdominal wall?
mu-9f5f0fd6.explanation: The tendinous intersections across rectus abdominis divide the muscle into segments and create its characteristic appearance.

mu-8818bd60.stem: Of the three flat muscles of the anterolateral abdominal wall, which is the most superficial?
mu-8818bd60.explanation: From superficial to deep: external oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis. The fibres of the external oblique run like 'hands in pockets' (downwards and forwards).

mu-20d486f6.stem: Between which two points does the inguinal ligament run?
options: Anterior superior iliac spine and pubic tubercle
Anterior inferior iliac spine and ischial tuberosity
mu-20d486f6.explanation: The inguinal ligament is the rolled-under lower border of the external oblique aponeurosis; it runs from the ASIS to the pubic tubercle and is an important landmark of the groin.

mu-ecbf1e9c.stem: Where does the linea alba run?
options: Along the lateral border of rectus
Between the ASIS and pubic tubercle
From the umbilicus to the costal margin
Between the xiphoid process and the pubic symphysis
mu-ecbf1e9c.explanation: The linea alba is the fibrous band between the two recti formed by the midline fusion of the aponeuroses of the abdominal muscles; the umbilicus lies on it.

mu-6e45f64a.stem: Which triangular muscle gives the shoulder its rounded contour?
mu-6e45f64a.explanation: Deltoid arises from the clavicle, acromion and spine of the scapula and inserts on the deltoid tuberosity; it gives the shoulder its rounded contour and abducts the arm.

mu-b57e5057.stem: Which muscles form the rotator cuff?
options: Deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor
Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis
Supraspinatus, teres major, teres minor and latissimus dorsi
Supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres major and subscapularis
Subscapularis, pectoralis minor, teres minor and deltoid
mu-b57e5057.explanation: The rotator cuff (SITS) is the dynamic stabiliser holding the humeral head in the glenoid. Teres major is not part of the rotator cuff.

mu-19bfd68a.stem: Which is the 'biceps' muscle on the front of the arm?
mu-19bfd68a.explanation: Biceps brachii is the two-headed muscle on the front of the arm; it flexes the elbow and is a powerful supinator of the forearm.
